newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes fall at end of month.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes fall at end of month.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices fell in with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Monday, with trade stagnant as traders squared books for next month, players said.
The region's main Alaska North Slope (ANS) seller declined to offer the grade Monday and buyers were seen balanced for April.
BP on Thursday sold 100,000 barrels of Alaska North Slope (ANS) to a small West Coast refiner for -$0.85 off WTI, traders said.
The shipment was too small to influence overall discounts, which remain -$0.91 off WTI. ANS was talked $20.34/20.54 a barrel, off 35 cents a barrel.
Other light grades were unchanged, with Line 63 prices holding at postings plus $0.95 to $1.00.
Outright prices for Kern River remained steady for the third-straight day. Kern River, a key heavy grade, ranged $15.00/15.10 a barrel.
